decision.observed_event: One carved dwarf lifts out of the fresco. It is a small stone key.

appraisal.label: interest
appraisal.cause: A careful search turns up a stone key.

improv_read.player_bid: Nik searches the carved dwarves and succeeds on Perception.
improv_read.connection: The gang does not know the key; Uktarl sees only a guest pulling at the wall and out of his control.
improv_read.kit_choice: Kit gives the discovery its tactile moment and keeps its purpose unstated.

public_brief.objective: Get the snooping visitor away from the wall and back under his eye.
public_brief.tactic: Mock the find as a pebble he does not care about and press the visitor to sit.
public_brief.visible_cue: The dealer watches the visitor's hands at the wall, card still in his fingers.
public_brief.player_opening: Nik can pocket the find, keep searching, or return to the table.
public_brief.reply_to: I search the little dwarf figures closely.
public_brief.kit_focus: Narrate the find as what Nik's fingers feel, then let the dealer dismiss it, which shows he does not know what it is.
public_brief.mirror: steady energy, standard, no humor: let the find land tactile and quiet

player_mood.cue: I search the little dwarf figures closely

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: Your fingers work along the singing dwarves one by one until a figure no taller than your thumb shifts under them. It comes free with a dry scrape: carved stone, cold, and on its underside a short notched shaft that was never meant to be part of any statue.

segments.speaker: Dealer
segments.text: Breaking the furniture now, little scholar? The dwarves will not miss one singer, I suppose. But a guest with busy hands makes my brothers nervous. Put your pebble in your pocket and come play, where I can admire your hands on the cards instead. Or do you mean to take the whole wall apart?

segments.speaker: Kit
segments.text: What do you do with it?
segments.reacts_to: Put your pebble in your pocket
